entries.name: draw_resolution_scale_x
entries.description:
Integer pixel width scale used for scaling the rendering resolution opaquely to the game.
Values from 1 to 7 may be supported, depending on device capabilities. Requires sparse binding (Vulkan) or tiled resources (D3D12) for scales above 1x1. The emulator will automatically clamp to the maximum supported scale if the requested value exceeds device limits.
Various effects and parts of game rendering pipelines may work incorrectly as pixels become ambiguous from the game's perspective and because half-pixel offset (which normally doesn't affect coverage when MSAA isn't used) becomes full-pixel.
entries.label: Escala de resolución horizontal

entries.name: draw_resolution_scale_y
entries.description:
Integer pixel width scale used for scaling the rendering resolution opaquely to the game.
See draw_resolution_scale_x for more information.
entries.label: Escala de resolución vertical

entries.name: vsync
entries.description: Enable VSYNC.
entries.label: Sincronización vertical
entries.help: Sincroniza la presentación con la pantalla.

entries.help: -1: selección automática. -2: renderizado WARP por software.

entries.description:
Decoder version used to process XMA audio.
Use: [fake, master, old, new]
 fake: 
  No audio will be decoded.
 master: 
  Version of decoder exactly like on base version of Xenia.
 old: 
  Decoder based on master version of decoder with few improvements.
 new: 
  New version of decoder. Provides highest stability, but isn't yet finished.
entries.label: Decodificador de audio XMA

entries.name: break_on_instruction
entries.description: int3 before the given guest address is executed.
entries.label: break on instruction

entries.name: break_on_start
entries.description: Break into the debugger on startup.
entries.label: break on start

entries.name: break_on_unimplemented_instructions
entries.description: Break to the host debugger (or crash if no debugger attached) if an unimplemented PowerPC instruction is encountered.
entries.label: break on unimplemented instructions

entries.name: clock_no_scaling
entries.description: Disable scaling code. Time management and locking is bypassed. Guest system time is directly pulled from host.
entries.label: clock no scaling

entries.name: clock_source_raw
entries.description: On x64, Use the RDTSC instruction as the time source. Requires invariant TSC. On a64, Use the CNTVCT_EL0 register as the time source
entries.label: clock source raw

entries.name: cpu
entries.description: Does nothing. CPU backend [any, x64].
entries.label: cpu

entries.name: debug_symbol_loader
entries.description: Enable dbghelp debug logging and validation.
entries.label: debug symbol loader

entries.name: debugprint_trap_log
entries.description: Log debugprint traps to the active debugger
entries.label: debugprint trap log

entries.name: disable_context_promotion
entries.description: Disables Context Promotion optimizations, this may be needed for some sports games, but will reduce performance.
entries.label: disable context promotion

entries.name: disable_instruction_infocache
entries.description: Disables caching records of called instructions/mmio accesses.
entries.label: disable instruction infocache

entries.name: disable_prefetch_and_cachecontrol
entries.description: Disables translating ppc prefetch/cache flush instructions to host prefetch/cacheflush instructions. This may improve performance as these instructions were written with the Xbox 360's cache in mind, and modern processors do their own automatic prefetching.
entries.label: disable prefetch and cachecontrol

entries.name: disassemble_functions
entries.description: Disassemble functions during generation.
entries.label: disassemble functions

entries.name: dump_translated_hir_functions
entries.description: dumps translated hir
entries.label: dump translated hir functions

entries.name: elide_e0_check
entries.description: Eliminate e0 check on some memory accesses, like to r13(tls) or r1(sp)
entries.label: elide e0 check

entries.name: emit_inline_mmio_checks
entries.description: Emit inline MMIO range checks for all I32 loads/stores instead of relying on exception-based MMIO detection.
entries.label: emit inline mmio checks

entries.name: emit_mmio_aware_stores_for_recorded_exception_addresses
entries.description: Uses info gathered via record_mmio_access_exceptions to emit special stores that are faster than trapping the exception
entries.label: emit mmio aware stores for recorded exception addresses

entries.name: emit_source_annotations
entries.description: Add extra movs and nops to make disassembly easier to read.
entries.label: emit source annotations

entries.name: enable_early_precompilation
entries.description: Enable pre-compiling guest functions that we know we've called/that we've recognized as being functions via simple heuristics, good for error finding/stress testing with the JIT
entries.label: enable early precompilation

entries.name: full_optimization_even_with_debug
entries.description: For developer use to analyze the quality of the generated code, not intended for actual debugging of the code
entries.label: full optimization even with debug

entries.name: ignore_trap_instructions
entries.description: Generate no code for powerpc trap instructions, can result in better performance in games that aggressively check with trap.
entries.label: ignore trap instructions

entries.name: ignore_undefined_externs
entries.description: Don't exit when an undefined extern is called.
entries.label: ignore undefined externs

entries.name: inline_loadclock
entries.description: Directly read cached guest clock without calling the LoadClock method (it gets repeatedly updated by calls from other threads)
entries.label: inline loadclock

entries.name: inline_mmio_access
entries.description: Inline constant MMIO loads and stores.
entries.label: inline mmio access

entries.name: load_module_map
entries.description: Loads a .map for symbol names and to diff with the generated symbol database.
entries.label: load module map

entries.name: no_reserved_ops
entries.description: For testing whether a game may have races with a broken reserved load/store impl
entries.label: no reserved ops

entries.name: no_round_to_single
entries.description: Not for users, breaks games. Skip rounding double values to single precision and back
entries.label: no round to single

entries.name: permit_float_constant_evaluation
entries.description: Allow float constant evaluation, may produce incorrect results and break games math
entries.label: permit float constant evaluation

entries.name: pvr
entries.description:
Known PVR's.
 0x710200 = Used by Zephyr 
 0x710300 = Used by Zephyr
 0x710500 = Used by Jasper
 0x710700 = Default
 0x710800 = Used by Corona V1 & V2
Processor version and revision number.
Bits 0 to 15 are the version number.
Bits 16 to 31 are the revision number.
Note: Some XEXs (such as mfgbootlauncher.xex) may check for a value that's less than 0x710700.
entries.label: pvr

entries.name: record_mmio_access_exceptions
entries.description: For guest addresses records whether we caught any mmio accesses for them. This info can then be used on a subsequent run to instruct the recompiler to emit checks
entries.label: record mmio access exceptions

entries.name: store_all_context_values
entries.description: Don't strip dead context stores to aid in debugging.
entries.label: store all context values

entries.name: trace_function_coverage
entries.description: Generate tracing for function instruction coverage statistics.
entries.label: trace function coverage

entries.name: trace_function_data
entries.description: Generate tracing for function result data.
entries.label: trace function data

entries.name: trace_function_data_path
entries.description: File to write trace data to.
entries.label: trace function data path

entries.name: trace_function_references
entries.description: Generate tracing for function address references.
entries.label: trace function references

entries.name: trace_functions
entries.description: Generate tracing for function statistics.
entries.label: trace functions

entries.name: use_fast_dot_product
entries.description: Use less accurate dot-product exception handling that converts all infinite results to QNaN.
entries.label: use fast dot product

entries.name: validate_hir
entries.description: Perform validation checks on the HIR during compilation.
entries.label: validate hir

entries.name: writable_code_segments
entries.description: Enables a program to write to its own code segments in memory.
entries.label: writable code segments

entries.name: defaults_date
entries.description: Do not modify - internal version of the default values in the config, for seamless updates if default value of any option is changed.
entries.label: Versión de valores predeterminados
entries.help: Dato interno del motor; solo lectura.

entries.name: license_mask
entries.description:
Set license mask for activated content.
 0 = No licenses enabled.
 1 = First license enabled. Generally the full version license in
     Xbox Live Arcade titles.
 -1 or 0xFFFFFFFF = All possible licenses enabled. Generally a
                    bad idea, could lead to undefined behavior.
entries.label: Máscara de licencias del contenido

entries.name: d3d12_allow_variable_refresh_rate_and_tearing
entries.description: In fullscreen, allow using variable refresh rate on displays supporting it. On displays not supporting VRR, screen tearing may occur in certain cases.
entries.label: d3d12 allow variable refresh rate and tearing

entries.name: d3d12_bindless
entries.description: Use bindless resources where available - may improve performance, but may make debugging more complicated.
entries.label: d3d12 bindless

entries.name: d3d12_break_on_error
entries.description: Break on Direct3D 12 validation errors.
entries.label: d3d12 break on error

entries.name: d3d12_break_on_warning
entries.description: Break on Direct3D 12 validation warnings.
entries.label: d3d12 break on warning

entries.name: d3d12_debug
entries.description: Enable Direct3D 12 and DXGI debug layer.
entries.label: d3d12 debug

entries.name: d3d12_dxbc_disasm
entries.description: Disassemble DXBC shaders after generation.
entries.label: d3d12 dxbc disasm

entries.name: d3d12_dxbc_disasm_dxilconv
entries.description: Disassemble DXBC shaders after conversion to DXIL, if DXIL shaders are supported by the OS, and DirectX Shader Compiler DLLs available at https://github.com/microsoft/DirectXShaderCompiler/releases are present.
entries.label: d3d12 dxbc disasm dxilconv

entries.name: d3d12_pipeline_creation_threads
entries.description: Number of threads used for graphics pipeline creation. -1 to calculate automatically (75% of logical CPU cores), a positive number to specify the number of threads explicitly (up to the number of logical CPU cores), 0 to disable multithreaded pipeline creation.
entries.label: d3d12 pipeline creation threads

entries.name: d3d12_queue_priority
entries.description: Graphics (direct) command queue scheduling priority, 0 - normal, 1 - high, 2 - global realtime (requires administrator privileges, may impact system responsibility)
entries.label: d3d12 queue priority

entries.name: d3d12_submit_on_primary_buffer_end
entries.description: Submit the command list when a PM4 primary buffer ends if it's possible to submit immediately to try to reduce frame latency.
entries.label: d3d12 submit on primary buffer end

entries.name: d3d12_tessellation_wireframe
entries.description: Display tessellated surfaces as wireframe for debugging.
entries.label: d3d12 tessellation wireframe

entries.name: host_present_from_non_ui_thread
entries.description: Allow the GPU emulation thread to present the guest output to the host surface directly instead of requesting the UI thread to do so through the host window system.
entries.label: host present from non ui thread

entries.name: postprocess_antialiasing
entries.description:
Post-processing anti-aliasing effect to apply to the image output of the game.
Using post-process anti-aliasing is heavily recommended when AMD FidelityFX Contrast Adaptive Sharpening or Super Resolution 1.0 is active.
Use: [none, fxaa, fxaa_extreme]
 none (or any value not listed here):
  Don't alter the original image.
 fxaa:
  NVIDIA Fast Approximate Anti-Aliasing 3.11, normal quality preset (12).
 fxaa_extreme:
  NVIDIA Fast Approximate Anti-Aliasing 3.11, extreme quality preset (39).
entries.label: Suavizado de bordes

entries.name: postprocess_dither
entries.description:
Dither the final image output from the internal precision to 8 bits per channel so gradients are smoother.
On a 10bpc display, the lower 2 bits will still be kept, but noise will be added to them - disabling may be recommended for 10bpc, but it depends on the 10bpc displaying capabilities of the actual display used.
entries.label: Suavizar gradientes de color

entries.name: postprocess_ffx_cas_additional_sharpness
entries.description:
Additional sharpness for AMD FidelityFX Contrast Adaptive Sharpening (CAS), from 0 to 1.
Higher is sharper.
entries.label: Nitidez adicional de CAS

entries.name: postprocess_ffx_fsr_max_upsampling_passes
entries.description:
Maximum number of upsampling passes performed in AMD FidelityFX Super Resolution 1.0 (FSR) before falling back to bilinear stretching after the final pass.
Each pass upscales only to up to 2x2 the previous size. If the game outputs a 1280x720 image, 1 pass will upscale it to up to 2560x1440 (below 4K), after 2 passes it will be upscaled to a maximum of 5120x2880 (including 3840x2160 for 4K), and so on.
This variable has no effect if the display resolution isn't very high, but may be reduced on resolutions like 4K or 8K in case the performance impact of multiple FSR upsampling passes is too high, or if softer edges are desired.
The default value is the maximum internally supported by Xenia.
entries.label: Pasadas máximas de FSR

entries.name: postprocess_ffx_fsr_sharpness_reduction
entries.description:
Sharpness reduction for AMD FidelityFX Super Resolution 1.0 (FSR), in stops.
Lower is sharper.
entries.label: Reducción de nitidez de FSR

entries.name: postprocess_scaling_and_sharpening
entries.description:
Post-processing effect to use for resampling and/or sharpening of the final display output.
Use: [bilinear, cas, fsr]
 bilinear (or any value not listed here):
  Original image at 1:1, simple bilinear stretching for resampling.
 cas:
  Use AMD FidelityFX Contrast Adaptive Sharpening (CAS) for sharpening at scaling factors of up to 2x2, with additional bilinear stretching for larger factors.
 fsr:
  Use AMD FidelityFX Super Resolution 1.0 (FSR) for highest-quality upscaling, or AMD FidelityFX Contrast Adaptive Sharpening for sharpening while not scaling or downsampling.
  For scaling by factors of more than 2x2, multiple FSR passes are done.
entries.label: Escalado y nitidez

entries.name: present_letterbox
entries.description: Maintain aspect ratio when stretching by displaying bars around the image when there's no more overscan area to crop out.
entries.label: Conservar relación de aspecto

entries.name: present_render_pass_clear
entries.description: On graphics backends where this is supported, use the clear render pass load operation in presentation instead of clear commands clearing only the letterbox area.
entries.label: present render pass clear

entries.name: present_safe_area_x
entries.description: Percentage of the image width that can be kept when presenting to maintain aspect ratio without letterboxing or stretching.
entries.label: Área visible horizontal (%)

entries.name: present_safe_area_y
entries.description: Percentage of the image height that can be kept when presenting to maintain aspect ratio without letterboxing or stretching.
entries.label: Área visible vertical (%)

entries.name: debug_msaa_2x_as_4x
entries.description: Use 4x MSAA with 2 samples instead of native 2x MSAA when available. For scalability testing on host GPU APIs where 2x is not mandatory. MSAA will be of a similar or worse quality and use more memory.
entries.label: debug msaa 2x as 4x

entries.name: depth_transfer_not_equal_test
entries.description:
When transferring data between depth render targets, use the "not equal" test to avoid writing rewriting depth via shader depth output if it's the same as the one currently in the depth buffer in case of round trips of the data.
Settings this to true may make transfer round trips more friendly to depth compression depending on how the GPU implements it (as arbitrary depth output may result in it being disabled completely), which is beneficial to subsequent rendering, while setting this to false may reduce bandwidth usage during transfers as the previous depth won't need to be read.
entries.label: depth transfer not equal test

entries.name: dump_shaders
entries.description: For shader debugging, path to dump GPU shaders to as they are compiled.
entries.label: dump shaders

entries.name: dxbc_source_map
entries.description: Disassemble Xenos instructions as comments in the resulting DXBC for debugging.
entries.label: dxbc source map

entries.name: dxbc_switch
entries.description: Use switch rather than if for flow control. Turning this off or on may improve stability, though this heavily depends on the driver - on AMD, it's recommended to have this set to true, as some titles appear to crash when if is used for flow control (possibly the shader compiler tries to flatten them). On Intel HD Graphics, this is ignored because of a crash with the switch instruction.
entries.label: dxbc switch

entries.name: execute_unclipped_draw_vs_on_cpu
entries.description:
Execute the vertex shader for draws with clipping disabled, primarily screen-space draws (such as clears), on the CPU when possible to estimate the extent of the EDRAM involved in the draw.
Enabling this may significantly improve GPU performance as otherwise up to the entire EDRAM may be considered used in draws without clipping, potentially resulting in spurious EDRAM range ownership transfer round trips between host render targets.
Also, on hosts where certain render target formats have to be emulated in a lossy way (for instance, 16-bit fixed-point via 16-bit floating-point), this prevents corruption of other render targets located after the current ones in the EDRAM by lossy range ownership transfers done for those draws.
entries.label: execute unclipped draw vs on cpu

entries.name: execute_unclipped_draw_vs_on_cpu_for_psi_render_backend
entries.description:
If execute_unclipped_draw_vs_on_cpu is enabled, execute the vertex shader for unclipped draws on the CPU even when using the pixel shader interlock (rasterizer-ordered view) implementation of the render backend on the host, for which no expensive copying between host render targets is needed when the ownership of a EDRAM range is changed.
If this is enabled, excessive barriers may be eliminated when switching between different render targets in separate EDRAM locations.
entries.label: execute unclipped draw vs on cpu for psi render backend

entries.name: execute_unclipped_draw_vs_on_cpu_with_scissor
entries.description:
Don't restrict the usage of execute_unclipped_draw_vs_on_cpu to only non-scissored draws (with the right and the bottom sides of the scissor rectangle at 8192 or beyond) even though if the scissor rectangle is present, it's usually sufficient for esimating the height of the render target.
Enabling this may cause excessive processing of vertices on the CPU, as some games draw rectangles (for their UI, for instance) without clipping, but with a proper scissor rectangle.
entries.label: execute unclipped draw vs on cpu with scissor

entries.name: force_convert_line_loops_to_strips
entries.description: For host graphics API downlevel support testing only, force CPU conversion of line loops to line strips even if the host supports line loop primitives natively.
entries.label: force convert line loops to strips

entries.name: force_convert_quad_lists_to_triangle_lists
entries.description:
For host graphics API downlevel support testing only, force CPU conversion of quad lists to quad strips even if the host supports quad list primitives natively or via geometry shader emulation.
May also be useful for graphics debugging when the debugger doesn't display the geometry generated by geometry shaders properly.
entries.label: force convert quad lists to triangle lists

entries.name: force_convert_triangle_fans_to_lists
entries.description: For host graphics API downlevel support testing only, force CPU conversion of triangle fans to triangle lists even if the host supports triangle fan primitives natively.
entries.label: force convert triangle fans to lists

entries.name: gamma_render_target_as_unorm16
entries.description: When the host can't write 8 bits per component pixels with piecewise linear gamma encoding directly with correct blending, use the 16-bit unsigned normalized format, if supported, for conceptually correct 8_8_8_8_GAMMA render target format blending in linear color space. Greatly increases accuracy for this format, but may result in render target copying costs if the game switches between 8_8_8_8_GAMMA and 8_8_8_8 views for the same EDRAM render target.
entries.label: gamma render target as unorm16

entries.name: half_pixel_offset
entries.description: Enable support of vertex half-pixel offset (D3D9 PA_SU_VTX_CNTL PIX_CENTER). Generally games are aware of the half-pixel offset, and having this enabled is the correct behavior (disabling this may significantly break post-processing in some games), but in certain games it might have been ignored, resulting in slight blurriness of UI textures, for instance, when they are read between texels rather than at texel centers, or the leftmost/topmost pixels may not be fully covered when MSAA is used with fullscreen passes.
entries.label: half pixel offset

entries.name: ignore_32bit_vertex_index_support
entries.description: For host graphics API downlevel testing only (useful only for Qualcomm Adreno 4xx-level host GPU testing), force indirection or pre-masking and pre-swapping of 32-bit vertex indices as if the host only supports 24-bit indices.
entries.label: ignore 32bit vertex index support

entries.name: mrt_edram_used_range_clamp_to_min
entries.description:
With host render targets, if multiple render targets are bound, estimate the EDRAM range modified in any of them to be not bigger than the distance between any two render targets in the EDRAM, rather than allowing the last one claim the rest of the EDRAM.
Has effect primarily on draws without viewport clipping.
Setting this to false results in higher accuracy in rare cases, but may increase the amount of copying that needs to be done sometimes.
entries.label: mrt edram used range clamp to min

entries.name: native_stencil_value_output_d3d12_intel
entries.description: Allow stencil reference output usage on Direct3D 12 on Intel GPUs - not working on UHD Graphics 630 as of March 2021 (driver 27.20.0100.8336).
entries.label: native stencil value output d3d12 intel

entries.name: no_discard_stencil_in_transfer_pipelines
entries.description: Skip stencil bit discard in render target transfer pipelines. May improve performance on some GPUs.
entries.label: no discard stencil in transfer pipelines

entries.name: non_seamless_cube_map
entries.description: Disable filtering between cube map faces near edges where possible (Vulkan with VK_EXT_non_seamless_cube_map) to reproduce the Direct3D 9 behavior.
entries.label: non seamless cube map

entries.name: primitive_processor_cache_min_indices
entries.description:
Smallest number of guest indices to store in the cache to try reusing later in the same frame if processing (such as primitive type conversion or reset index replacement) is performed.
Setting this to a very high value may result in excessive CPU processing, while a very low value may result in excessive locking and lookups.
Negative values disable caching.
entries.label: primitive processor cache min indices

entries.name: snorm16_render_target_full_range
entries.description: When the host can only support 16_16 and 16_16_16_16 render targets as -1...1, remap -32...32 to -1...1 to use the full possible range of values, at the expense of multiplicative blending correctness.
entries.label: snorm16 render target full range

entries.name: store_shaders
entries.description: Store shaders persistently and load them when loading games to avoid runtime spikes and freezes when playing the game not for the first time.
entries.label: store shaders

entries.name: target_trace_file
entries.description: Specifies the trace file to load.
entries.label: target trace file

entries.name: texture_cache_memory_limit_hard
entries.description: Maximum host texture memory usage (in megabytes) above which textures will be destroyed as soon as possible.
entries.label: texture cache memory limit hard

entries.name: texture_cache_memory_limit_render_to_texture
entries.description:
Part of the host texture memory budget (in megabytes) that will be scaled by the current drawing resolution scale.
If texture_cache_memory_limit_soft, for instance, is 384, and this is 24, it will be assumed that the game will be using roughly 24 MB of render-to-texture (resolve) targets and 384 - 24 = 360 MB of regular textures - so with 2x2 resolution scaling, the soft limit will be 360 + 96 MB, and with 3x3, it will be 360 + 216 MB.
entries.label: texture cache memory limit render to texture

entries.name: texture_cache_memory_limit_soft
entries.description: Maximum host texture memory usage (in megabytes) above which old textures will be destroyed.
entries.label: texture cache memory limit soft

entries.name: texture_cache_memory_limit_soft_lifetime
entries.description: Seconds a texture should be unused to be considered old enough to be deleted if texture memory usage exceeds texture_cache_memory_limit_soft.
entries.label: texture cache memory limit soft lifetime

entries.name: tiled_shared_memory
entries.description: Enable tiled/sparse resources for efficient large address space support. Disable for graphics debugger compatibility.
entries.label: tiled shared memory

entries.name: trace_dump_path
entries.description: Output path for dumped files.
entries.label: trace dump path

entries.name: trace_gpu_prefix
entries.description: Prefix path for GPU trace files.
entries.label: trace gpu prefix

entries.name: trace_gpu_stream
entries.description: Trace all GPU packets.
entries.label: trace gpu stream

entries.name: anisotropic_override
entries.description:
Forces anisotropic filtering (AF) for eligible textures.
Higher values keep textures sharper at oblique angles at the cost of GPU bandwidth, though most GPUs handle up to 16x fine.
In rare cases, forcing AF can introduce visual artifacts.
 -1 = No override
  0 = Disable anisotropic filtering
  1 = Force 1x anisotropic filtering
  2 = Force 2x anisotropic filtering
  3 = Force 4x anisotropic filtering
  4 = Force 8x anisotropic filtering
  5 = Force 16x anisotropic filtering
entries.label: Filtrado anisotrópico

entries.name: async_shader_compilation
entries.description: Compile shaders and create pipelines asynchronously in background threads. Eliminates shader compilation stutter but may cause brief rendering artifacts while pipelines are being created. When disabled, pipelines are created synchronously which causes stutter but no visual artifacts.
entries.label: Compilación asíncrona de shaders
entries.help: Reduce pausas de compilación; puede mostrar artefactos mientras se preparan los shaders.

entries.name: clear_memory_page_state
entries.description: Refresh state of memory pages to enable gpu written data. (Use for 'Team Ninja' Games to fix missing character models)
entries.label: clear memory page state

entries.name: depth_bias_shader_offset
entries.description: Route decal host render target draws with polygon offset through shader depth. This avoids Z-fighting in games that rely on tiny depth bias values that host fixed function depth bias cannot reproduce reliably.This likely causes some minor performance penalty, but the cost should be minimal if only a small portion of the scene is affected.
entries.label: depth bias shader offset

entries.name: depth_float24_convert_in_pixel_shader
entries.description:
Whether to convert the depth values to 24-bit floating-point (20e4) from the host precision (32-bit floating point) directly in the pixel shaders of guest draws when using a host depth buffer.
This prevents visual artifacts (interleaved stripes of parts of surfaces rendered and parts not rendered, having either the same width in case of the "greater or equal" depth test function, or the former being much thinner than the latter with the "equal" function) if the full host precision depth data is lost.
This issue may happen if the game reloads the depth data previously evicted from the EDRAM to the RAM back to the EDRAM, but the EDRAM region that previously contained that depth buffer was overwritten by another depth buffer, or the game loads it to a different location in the EDRAM than it was previously placed at, thus Xenia is unable to restore the depth data with the original precision, and instead falls back to converting the lower-precision values, so in subsequent rendering passes for the same geometry, the actual depth values of the surfaces don't match those stored in the depth buffer anymore.
This is a costly option because it makes the GPU unable to use depth buffer compression, and also with MSAA, forces the pixel shader to run for every subpixel sample rather than for the entire pixel, making pixel shading 2 or 4 times heavier depending on the MSAA sample count.
The rounding direction is controlled by the depth_float24_round configuration variable.
Note that with depth_float24_round = true, this becomes even more costly because pixel shaders must be executed regardless of whether the surface is behind the previously drawn surfaces. With depth_float24_round = false, conservative depth output is used, however, so depth rejection before the pixel shader may still work.
If sample-rate shading is not supported by the host GPU, the conversion in the pixel shader is done only when MSAA is not used.
When the depth buffer is emulated in software (via the fragment shader interlock / rasterizer-ordered view), this is ignored because 24-bit depth is always used directly.
entries.label: depth float24 convert in pixel shader

entries.name: depth_float24_round
entries.description:
Whether to round to the nearest even, rather than truncating (rounding towards zero), the depth when converting it to 24-bit floating-point (20e4) from the host precision (32-bit floating point) when using a host depth buffer.
false:
 Recommended.
 The conversion may move the depth values farther away from the camera.
 Without depth_float24_convert_in_pixel_shader:
  The "greater or equal" depth test function continues to work fine if the full host precision depth data is lost, it's still possible to draw another pass of the same geometry with it.
  (See the description of depth_float24_convert_in_pixel_shader for more information about full precision depth data loss.)
 With depth_float24_convert_in_pixel_shader:
  Faster - the pixel shader for hidden surfaces may still be skipped (using conservative depth output).
true:
 Only for special cases of issues caused by minor 32-bit floating-point rounding errors, for instance, when the game tries to draw something at the camera plane by setting Z of the vertex position to W.
 The conversion may move the depth values closer or farther.
 Using the same rounding mode as in the Direct3D 9 reference rasterizer.
 Without depth_float24_convert_in_pixel_shader:
  Not possible to recover from a full host precision depth data loss - in subsequent passes of rendering the same geometry, half of the samples will be failing the depth test with the "greater or equal" depth test function.
 With depth_float24_convert_in_pixel_shader:
  Slower - depth rejection before the pixel shader is not possible.
When the depth buffer is emulated in software (via the fragment shader interlock / rasterizer-ordered view), this is ignored, and rounding to the nearest even is always done.
entries.label: depth float24 round

entries.name: draw_resolution_scale_threshold
entries.description:
Surface pitch in pixels at or below render targets skip being upscaled by draw_resolution_scale_x/y. 0 disables it.
Small offscreen surfaces like bloom or depth of field buffers often break when upscaled and keeping them native avoids that. The pitch is compared after alignment to 80 pixel EDRAM tiles, so prefer conservative values, only as high as the broken effects need.
Host render targets only.
entries.label: draw resolution scale threshold

entries.name: occlusion_query
entries.description:
Controls hardware occlusion query behavior for EVENT_WRITE_ZPD.
Used for effects like lens flares, object culling, and auto-exposure.
 fake: Write a fake result without asking the GPU. Safe for most games,
       though some effects may look slightly wrong.
 fast: Ask the GPU but don't wait for the answer. Writes a cached
       result immediately and updates it when the GPU catches up.
       Cached results bias toward visible when guessing. (default)
 fast-alt: Variant of fast mode that keeps cached zero results for
           unresolved reports. May improve effects relying on precise
           visibility, but may be less stable for occlusion culling.
 strict: Ask the GPU and wait for the real result before continuing.
         Most accurate, but may be somewhat less performant.
entries.label: occlusion query

entries.name: occlusion_query_fake_lower_threshold
entries.description:
Lower end of the fake sample count value written on EVENT_WRITE_ZPD when real occlusion queries are disabled.
-1 writes nothing, resulting in some games that sit and hang.
0 means the fake result stays fully occluded.
entries.label: occlusion query fake lower threshold

entries.name: occlusion_query_fake_upper_threshold
entries.description:
Upper end of the fake sample count value written on EVENT_WRITE_ZPD when real occlusion queries are disabled.
Keep this higher than occlusion_query_fake_lower_threshold.
Ignored if occlusion_query_fake_lower_threshold is -1.
entries.label: occlusion query fake upper threshold

entries.name: occlusion_query_querybatch_range
entries.description:
Range of fake sample count values to walk for titles using the D3D QueryBatch standard before wrapping back to occlusion_query_fake_lower_threshold.
This shouldn't be changed from the default value of 0 (disabled) unless necessary for a specific title.
entries.label: occlusion query querybatch range

entries.name: occlusion_query_saturation
entries.description:
Compress higher occlusion query sample counts before guest writeback.
This can be useful if effects such as lens flares appear too strong.
1.0 = default behavior
0.0 = collapse all nonzero sample counts to 1
Values around 0.90 are a good starting point for subtle tuning.
entries.label: occlusion query saturation

entries.name: readback_memexport
entries.description: Read data written by memory export in shaders on the CPU. This may be needed in some games (but many only access exported data on the GPU, and this flag isn't needed to handle such behavior), but causes mid-frame synchronization, so it has a huge performance impact.
entries.label: readback memexport

entries.name: readback_resolve
entries.description:
Controls CPU readback of render-to-texture resolve results.
 fast: Read from previous frame (1 frame delay, no GPU stall, slight performance hit)
 full: Wait for GPU to finish (accurate but slow, GPU-CPU sync stall)
 none: Disable readback completely (some games render better without it)
entries.label: readback resolve

entries.name: readback_resolve_half_pixel_offset
entries.description:
When resolution scaling and readback resolve are enabled, resolve downscaling keeps one supersample out of each scaled pixel block.
This selects the center of the block instead of the top-left corner, which can be closer to where the GPU would have sampled the original pixel, and can help with thin features and edge coverage.
Both choices give a real rendered value, but they can disagree where geometry edges fall inside a pixel block.
This matters when the CPU reads the resolve as data instead of an image, such as for gamma correction readbacks, occlusion checks, and GPU buffers reused later in the frame.
entries.label: readback resolve half pixel offset

entries.name: render_target_path_d3d12
entries.description:
Render target emulation path to use on Direct3D 12.
Use: [any, rtv, rov]
 rtv:
  Host render targets and fixed-function blending and depth / stencil testing, copying between render targets when needed.
  Lower accuracy (limited pixel format support).
  Performance limited primarily by render target layout changes requiring copying, but generally higher.
 rov:
  Manual pixel packing, blending and depth / stencil testing, with free render target layout changes.
  Requires a GPU supporting rasterizer-ordered views.
  Highest accuracy (all pixel formats handled in software).
  Performance limited primarily by overdraw.
  On AMD drivers, currently causes shader compiler crashes in many cases.
 Any other value:
  Choose what is considered the most optimal for the system (currently always RTV because the ROV path is much slower now, except for Intel GPUs, which have a bug in stencil testing that causes Xbox 360 Direct3D 9 clears not to work).
entries.label: Ruta de renderizado Direct3D 12

entries.name: render_target_path_vulkan
entries.description:
Render target emulation path to use on Vulkan.
Use: [any, fbo, fsi]
 fbo:
  Host framebuffers and fixed-function blending and depth / stencil testing, copying between render targets when needed.
  Lower accuracy (limited pixel format support).
  Performance limited primarily by render target layout changes requiring copying, but generally higher.
 fsi:
  Manual pixel packing, blending and depth / stencil testing, with free render target layout changes.
  Requires a GPU supporting fragment shader interlock.
  Highest accuracy (all pixel formats handled in software).
  Performance limited primarily by overdraw.
 Any other value:
  Choose what is considered the most optimal for the system (currently always FB because the FSI path is much slower now).
entries.label: Ruta de renderizado Vulkan

entries.description: Enable sparse binding for shared memory emulation. Disabling it increases video memory usage - a 512 MB buffer is created - but allows graphics debuggers that don't support sparse binding to work.
entries.label: vulkan sparse shared memory

entries.name: vulkan_validation
entries.description: Enable the Vulkan validation layer (VK_LAYER_KHRONOS_validation). Messages will be written to the Xenia log if 'vulkan_log_debug_messages' is enabled, or to the OS debug output otherwise.
entries.label: vulkan validation

entries.name: win32_high_resolution_timer
entries.description: Requests high-resolution timer from the NT kernel
entries.label: win32 high resolution timer

entries.name: win32_mmcss
entries.description: Opt in the Multimedia Class Scheduler Service (MMCSS) scheduling for prioritized access to CPU resources
entries.label: win32 mmcss

entries.name: align_all_basic_blocks
entries.description: Aligns the start of all basic blocks to N bytes. Only specify a power of 2, 16 is the recommended value. Results in larger icache usage, but potentially faster loops
entries.label: align all basic blocks

entries.name: delay_via_maybeyield
entries.description: implement the db16cyc instruction via MaybeYield, may improve scheduling of guest threads
entries.label: delay via maybeyield

entries.name: enable_host_guest_stack_synchronization
entries.description: Records entries for guest/host stack mappings at function starts and checks for reentry at return sites. Has slight performance impact, but fixes crashes in games that use setjmp/longjmp.
entries.label: enable host guest stack synchronization

entries.name: enable_incorrect_roundingmode_behavior
entries.description: Disables the FPU/VMX MXCSR sharing workaround, potentially causing incorrect rounding behavior and denormal handling in VMX code. The workaround may cause reduced CPU performance but is a more accurate emulation
entries.label: enable incorrect roundingmode behavior

entries.name: enable_rmw_context_merging
entries.description: Permit merging read-modify-write HIR instr sequences together into x86 instructions that use a memory operand.
entries.label: enable rmw context merging

entries.name: instrument_call_times
entries.description: Compute time taken for functions, for profiling guest code
entries.label: instrument call times

entries.name: max_stackpoints
entries.description: Max number of host->guest stack mappings we can record.
entries.label: max stackpoints

entries.name: x64_extension_mask
entries.description:
Allow the detection and utilization of specific instruction set features.
    0 = x86_64 + AVX1
    1 = AVX2
    2 = FMA
    4 = LZCNT
    8 = BMI1
   16 = BMI2
   32 = F16C
   64 = Movbe
  128 = GFNI
  256 = AVX512F
  512 = AVX512VL
 1024 = AVX512BW
 2048 = AVX512DQ
 4096 = AVX512VBMI
   -1 = Detect and utilize all possible processor features
entries.label: x64 extension mask
